articles.headline: Vikings RB Aaron Jones working through knee injury
articles.description: The Vikings' offensive backfield is in flux this week as starter Aaron Jones Sr. works through a knee injury and backup Jordan Mason remains on injured reserve.
articles.headlineJa: バイキングスRBアーロン・ジョーンズ、膝の負傷を抱え調整中
articles.descriptionJa: 先発のアーロン・ジョーンズ・シニアが膝の負傷に対応しており、控えのジョーダン・メイソンが故障者リストに入ったままのため、今週のバイキングスのオフェンシブ・バックフィールドは流動的な状態にある。
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. -- The Minnesota Vikings' offensive backfield is in flux this week as starter Aaron Jones Sr. works through a knee injury and backup Jordan Mason remains on injured reserve.

The team planned to hold Jones out of practice Wednesday, coach Kevin O'Connell said, leaving only one running back on its roster who spent time with the team in training camp: rookie Demond Claiborne. Since then, the Vikings have signed three veterans: DeeJay Dallas, Jerome Ford and Jaret Patterson. As of Wednesday, Ford and Patterson were on the practice squad. Dallas was promoted to the 53-man roster last week.

Jones, 31, is coming off one of his best games in years after carrying 23 times for 105 yards in the Vikings' 9-3 victory over the Chicago Bears. He said afterward that he finished the game while wearing a knee brace. Jones also had a bruise on his left cheek after absorbing a violent hit to the helmet from Bears cornerback Tyrique Stevenson, one that knocked his helmet off.

O'Connell said that Jones feels "pretty good" but gave no indication whether he will be ready to play in the Vikings' game Sunday at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

"We'll just keep getting treatment around the clock," O'Connell said, "and see if we can pick up his workload as the week goes on."

Jones' status is especially notable given the absence of Mason, who fractured his thumb two weeks ago. The Vikings entered the season with Claiborne as their No. 3 back, but he was inactive in Week 1 and got only two snaps in Week 2. Both were pass plays designed for him to get the ball in space. He caught one for 2 yards, and quarterback Carson Wentz scrambled on the other play.

Dallas got two carries and gained 8 yards against the Bears.

articles.headline: In reversal, Chargers not placing Charlie Kolar (forearm) on IR
articles.description: In a surprising reversal, the Chargers are not placing tight end Charlie Kolar on injured reserve after he injured his left forearm in Sunday's game.
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- In a surprising reversal, the Los Angeles Chargers are not placing tight end Charlie Kolar on injured reserve after he injured his left forearm in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.

Coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that Kolar would go on injured reserve along with tight end David Njoku, but Kolar's surgery Monday changed his prognosis, and he will remain on the active roster.

Still, Harbaugh said Wednesday that Kolar won't play Sunday against the Buffalo Bills, or practice Wednesday.

With just one healthy tight end on the active roster in Oronde Gadsden, the Chargers signed tight end Hayden Rucci on Tuesday, poaching him from Jacksonville's practice squad.

Rucci is familiar with this Chargers system, having played four games in Miami last season under Mike McDaniel, now offensive coordinator for the Chargers. 

Rucci will likely be ready to contribute as early as Sunday and could be a big help in getting Los Angeles' struggling offense back on track. Gadsden struggles as a run blocker, which puts the offense at a significant disadvantage. Having Rucci, who is already familiar with the system and thrives as a blocker, gives this offense some hope to be multidimensional.

articles.headline: Nats' Cade Cavalli gets $4M lockout-shielded signing bonus
articles.description: Nationals pitcher Cade Cavalli will get a $4 million signing bonus as part of his new deal which will be shielded from losses from a possible lockout.
articles.body:
WASHINGTON -- Washington Nationals pitcher Cade Cavalli receives a $4 million signing bonus on Nov. 30 as part of a $47 million, four-year contract covering 2027-30, a payment shielded from potential losses caused by a possible lockout.

Cavalli gets salaries of $4 million next year, $7 million in 2028, $10 million in 2029 and $20 million in 2030 as part of the deal announced Friday.

Washington has a $25 million team option for 2031 with a $2 million buyout.

His 2030 salary could escalate by $5 million based on his finish in Cy Young Award voting and his 2031 option price could go up by a maximum $7.5 million, with 2029 voting impacting both years and 2030 affecting the following season.

Winning a Cy Young would trigger a $5 million boost, finishing second would be worth $2.5 million, third $1 million, fourth $750,000 and fifth $500,000.

Cavalli agreed in January to a one-year deal guaranteeing $862,500: an $862,500 salary this year and a $4 million team option for 2027 with a $7,500 buyout. As part of the superseding contract, he will not receive the buyout.

Cavalli would have been eligible for free agency after the 2029 season.

articles.headline: Sources: Extension unlikely as Knicks, Karl-Anthony Towns talks stall
articles.description: Extension talks have stagnated between the Knicks and Karl-Anthony Towns, and an agreement is considered unlikely as the team begins camp, sources told ESPN.
articles.body:
Talks have stagnated between the New York Knicks and Karl-Anthony Towns on a contract extension, and an agreement is considered unlikely as the team begins training camp next week, sources told ESPN on Wednesday.

The sides have spent extensive time discussing a potential extension during the offseason, but there has been no movement lately in negotiations, sources said, as the Knicks stand to go for a repeat following their first NBA title in 53 years.

Towns, who will turn 31 in mid-November, is eligible to receive a contract extension for up to four years and $273 million, according to ESPN's Bobby Marks.

An All-Star in his two seasons in New York, Towns averaged 15.9 points, 10.6 rebounds and 4.9 assists on 55% shooting through last season's playoffs, helping the Knicks to a 16-3 mark as they defeated the San Antonio Spurs in five games in the NBA Finals.

Knicks owner James Dolan has repeatedly said he wanted to keep the Knicks out of the punitive second apron. Valuable backup center Mitchell Robinson was one of the casualties of the edict, as he signed with the Boston Celtics this offseason.

Towns is due $57 million this season and has a $61 million player option for 2027-28. As it stands, the Knicks and Towns could come to an agreement at any point this season, but it is not imminent and appears unlikely in the short-term.

The Knicks have many looming contract decisions over the next several months. Swingman Josh Hart is eligible for a contract extension as well, while Jalen Brunson and OG Anunoby will be eligible for contract extensions next offseason.

articles.headline: 2026 NBA buzz: Latest free agency and trade updates
articles.description: We're tracking deals, trades and buzz across the NBA, including Pelle Larsson getting a long-term extension with the Heat.
articles.body:
NBA free agency has almost reached the end, with several players landing in new homes this offseason.

LeBron James decided to continue his historic career with the Philadelphia 76ers after months of deliberation. The Sixers also traded for Jaylen Brown this summer, turning the franchise into a true contender with two huge moves.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo is headed to South Beach to team up with Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers have been sold for the second time in 10 months.

What will happen next during this turbulent offseason?

Sept. 23

Extension unlikely as Knicks, Towns talks stall

Talks have stagnated between the New York Knicks and Karl-Anthony Towns on a contract extension, and an agreement is considered unlikely as the team begins training camp next week, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania and Vincent Goodwill on Wednesday.

The sides have spent extensive time discussing a potential extension during the offseason, but there has been no movement lately in negotiations, sources said, as the Knicks stand to go for a repeat following their first NBA title in 53 years.

Sept. 22

Charania: Hield, Nembhard to Charlotte for Finney-Smith

The Atlanta Hawks are trading Dorian Finney-Smith to the Charlotte Hornets for Buddy Hield, Ryan Nembhard and cash, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Leonard, Raptors agree to two-year extension

The Toronto Raptors and Kawhi Leonard have agreed to a two-year, $115 million extension, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Leonard now has a total of three years and $165 million left on his deal.

The 2026-27 season will be Leonard's first back in Toronto since the 2018-19 campaign, a season in which he helped lead the Raptors to their only title in franchise history.

Sept. 21

Charania: Pistons, Duren at an "impasse"

Free agent center Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons are at an impasse this season and the franchise is uncertain if he will show up to next Monday's Media Day, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

"When you talk to people close to [Duren], he feels a certain way toward the Pistons' respect level for him," Charania said on NBA Today. "For him it's been all about respect, for the team it has just been about business. ... Over the course of this offseason, his offer has been been around the $180 to $190 million over five years range. And that has also included incentives like weight clauses to my understanding. And that has all played a part in this as well.

"Over the last several weeks it's kind of quiet on this front. The sides have picked up communication. And I am told right now the Pistons offer to Jalen Duren is $200 million over five years."

Duren has until Oct. 1 to sign a qualifying offer.

articles.headline: Lamar Jackson, Ravens not focusing on field conditions in Rio
articles.description: A day before the Ravens travel to Brazil to play the Cowboys, quarterback Lamar Jackson said he isn't focusing on the condition of the field at Maracanã Stadium.
articles.headlineJa: ラマー・ジャクソンとレイブンズ、リオのピッチコンディションには囚われず
articles.descriptionJa: レイブンズがカウボーイズとの試合のためにブラジルへ渡る前日、クォーターバック（QB）のラマー・ジャクソンは、マラカナン・スタジアムのグラウンド状態には特に意識を向けていないと語った。
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- A day before the Baltimore Ravens travel to Brazil, quarterback Lamar Jackson said he isn't focusing on the condition of the field at Maracanã Stadium.

"I believe the NFL does a great job at having their specialists go out there and look over the fields," Jackson said Wednesday. "I cannot worry about that. I just have to worry about getting us a dub in Brazil. [As for] the field, we have played on bad fields plenty of times, so I cannot really dwell on that."

On Sunday, Baltimore plays the Dallas Cowboys in the NFL's first game in Rio de Janeiro.

The concerns about the quality of the playing surface at Rio's Maracanã Stadium started last week when professional soccer players voiced complaints about their home stadium's grass field. On Monday, NFL field director Nick Pappas told ESPN that there are "no concerns right now" about the field conditions in Rio.

Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton has heard about the criticism about the playing surface.

"There is a lot of just, 'he said, she said,' kind of thing going on right now, so we will see," Hamilton said. "I know the players are the product in this league. As soon as we lose 'putting the players forward' is when we lose the league. I am sure the league knows that and they are doing their best to put us in the position to be safe. So, that is not really in the forefront of my mind right now."

This is the Ravens' first international game since 2023, when they beat the Tennessee Titans 24-16 in London. The Ravens spent the entire week in England to prepare for that game.

For this trip, the Ravens and Cowboys are both flying to Brazil on Thursday night and will arrive Friday, which is two days before the game. The reason Baltimore isn't leaving earlier is because it's only a one-hour time difference.

"I feel like the rhetoric around the game after it is done is who handled the travel and everything better," Hamilton said. "I think that just goes hand in hand on who is being more of a pro or not. That is something that I think we can thrive at. So, I'm excited."

Two Cowboys played in the 2024 game in Sao Paolo and one of their coaches was involved in defensive tackle Kenny Clark, edge rusher Rashan Gary, who were with the Packers, and defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who was with the Eagles.

"It was mushy a little bit," Clark said of the field. "That was in Sao Paulo, so I wonder how the field in Rio is going to look, but yeah, that was a problem last time."

He added, "Of course, I hope it's good, but regardless we're playing on it, so I've got full confidence in the league doing their part and making sure the field is right. And my job is to go out there and put on a great performance."

Coach Brian Schottenheimer said the players have been educated on cleat choice. The team will have their molded cleats as well as the seven-stud shoes that could provide better traction.

articles.headline: Bills' T.J. Sanders out indefinitely after having appendectomy
articles.description: Bills defensive lineman T.J. Sanders is out indefinitely after having an appendectomy, coach Joe Brady said on Wednesday.
articles.headlineJa: ビルズのT.J.サンダース、虫垂切除手術を受け無期限離脱
articles.descriptionJa: ビルズのディフェンシブラインマン、T.J.サンダースが虫垂切除手術を受け無期限で離脱すると、ジョー・ブレディHCが水曜日に明かした。
articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- Buffalo Bills defensive lineman T.J. Sanders is out indefinitely after having an appendectomy, coach Joe Brady said on Wednesday.

Brady didn't provide a timetable on Sanders' return in announcing the player had surgery a day earlier. The second-year player was a projected starter, and has yet to appear in a game this season after missing Buffalo's first two games with a knee injury.

Buffalo (2-0) has been off since a 41-31 win over Detroit on Thursday, and hosts the Los Angeles Chargers (0-2) on Sunday.

Brady didn't have an update on receiver DJ Moore (shoulder) and defensive tackle Ed Oliver (hip). Moore was hurt during the game against Detroit, while Oliver was hurt during pregame warmups.

The Bills also signed defensive lineman Austin Johnson to their practice squad. Johnson previously played with Buffalo in 2024. He fills the spot left open after Miami signed linebacker Andre Jones on Tuesday.
